outcome: Diminished hydroxylation of type I collagen telopeptide lysines
Dominance of allysine aldol dimeric cross-links
cohort: The study involved a 4-year-old boy diagnosed with Bruck syndrome caused by compound heterozygous mutations in PLOD2.
finding: The primary finding was that bone from the patient with PLOD2 mutations exhibited diminished hydroxylation of type I collagen telopeptide lysines, resulting in the absence of stable trivalent cross-links and a dominance of allysine aldol dimeric cross-links.
cross-section timing: Observations were taken when the participant was 4 years old.
